To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

firms that are more productive, invest more in knowledge, are more likely to engage in globalisation, and that firms that are engaged in FDI have higher productivity than domestic firms, and are more likely to be engaged in exporting than domestic firms.

1. Firms that engage in FDI are different from domestic and exporting firms in terms of their knowledge investments, and that 2. FDI is an important mode of globalisation and is integral part of the globalisation process of firms in developing country context.

1) Firms that invest abroad are significantly different than domestic firms, in terms of productivity and knowledge investment; 2) Firms investing abroad have higher productivity than exporting firms; and 3) There is a strong positive association between productivity and the mode of globalisation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between firm productivity, globalisation activities, and knowledge investments.
the relationship between firm productivity, different modes of globalising and firm characteristics.
the relationship between productivity and different modes and degrees of globalisation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FDI is a part of the evolutionary ladder of firms in developing economies, but it is not a necessary condition for graduating from domestic to exporting and then to globalising firms.
FDI by Indian firms is an integral part in their globalisation process.
FDI is not a random phenomenon, but a natural and integral part of the evolutionary process of firms in developing economies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
FDI by firms is a natural progression in the evolution of firms and not an aberration.
the firms in developing countries that engage in FDI are more efficient, and that FDI is not a one-time phenomenon but a continuous process.
FDI is a natural extension of the export ladder for firms in developing countries, and that the presence of FDI in a country is an important determinant of firm productivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FDI is not just a strategy to expand sales and market access but is a part of a broader globalisation strategy of firms.
firms in developing countries that engage in FDI are not a random subset of the firms in the economy.
FDI is an important part of the ladder of globalisation, and firms that engage in FDI are more likely to be more productive.
